newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-What's Happening in Australian Sport.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-What's Happening in Australian Sport.

text.p: The most famous finger in Australian sport comes under increased scrutiny from Friday when Shane Warne leads Victoria in a Sheffield Shield cricket match against New South Wales at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Recent unsuccessful tours to India and Sri Lanka by Australia have underscored Warne's value to the national side, with local and international media now beginning to speculate whether the unofficial world champions can win without their star leg-spinner.
The match against New South Wales is Warne's first first-class fixture since he underwent surgery to repair ligament damage on the ring finger of his right hand in May.
His much-discussed digit has only had two light workouts in interstate limited overs matches in the past month for a total return of seven wickets for 90 runs from 20 overs.

The man himself said this week he was eager to test his finger in the rigours of Sheffield Shield cricket and the match against New South Wales should give a good indication whether Warne will be able to lead Australia through a hectic schedule of international cricket over the coming 12 months.
Australia's first opponents of the summer have already arrived, with West Indies taking on Western Australia in a three-day match in Perth from Friday.

The West Indians had a pretty forgettable start to the tour, losing to an Australian Cricket Board XI last week and then being beaten by nine wickets by Western Australia in a one day match on Wednesday.
Courtney Walsh and his men scored their first win on Thursday when they squeezed past Western Australia by one wicket in a return limited overs match.
Mike Gatting's England A are also in Australia and are playing South Australia in a three-day match which starts on Friday and ends on Monday.
In other Sheffield Shield action, David Boon's Tasmania were in deep trouble on the third day of their match against Queensland on Friday.
Tasmania were down two wickets in their second innings at lunch on Friday and were still 38 runs behind Queensland's first innings total of 244.
West Indies fly off to Alice Spings for a limited overs match against a Northern Territories XI on Tuesday before taking on an Australian XI in Hobart in a four-day match beginning next Friday.
Also starting next Friday are Sheffield Shield matches between Victoria and South Australia, New South Wales and Queensland and Western Australia against Tasmania.
The next few days will therefore be a good form guide for Warne, Australia and the Windies in the lead-up to the first test, which begins in Brisbane on November 22.
RUGBY UNION
Australia's battle-scarred Wallabies move on to Murrayfield on Saturday for the test against Scotland.
Undefeated so far on their tour of Europe, the Wallabies have suffered an astonishing run of bad luck with injuries and have had to fly in five new players to compensate for injuries to seven others.
The Scotland match will be Australia's first real test on tour after a relatively easy win over Italy and a series of matches against provincial sides.

The test is already significant for the decision by the Australia selectors to drop winger David Campese, whose star appears to be fading fast after the world-record try scorer played his 100th test against Italy last month.
Campese has been replaced by Australian Capital Territory winger Joe Roff.
On Wednesday Australia take on Connacht in Galway at the start of the Irish leg of their tour.
GOLF

The Australian Women's Open continues at the Yarra Yarra course in Melbourne until Sunday, with Australia's Karrie Webb looking to add her first home title to last year's British Open and three U.S. Tour victories this year.
Webb started Friday's second round four shots behind compatriot Corinne Dibnah, who led with Mardi Lunn after first rounds of 68.
The men's action gets underway next Thursday with the start of the Australian PGA championship in Sydney.
